Fourteenth Indian Expedition to Antarctica, Scientific Report, 1998 
Department of Ocean Development, Technical Publication No. 12, pp. 127-152 
Field  Relations  and  Petrological  Studies  of  Rocks  from
Conrad  Mountains,  Central  Dronning  Maud  Land,
East  Antarctica
B.R. BEJARNIYA, V. RAVIKANT and AMITAVA KUNDU
Antarctica Division
Geological Survey of India, Faridabad
Abstract
The deformational, metamorphic and plutonic history of Conrad range reveals earlier
high grade layered tonalitic gneiss probably representing part of basement of the area, which
preserve evidence of MI/DI event. They have been intruded by foliated charnockites
syntectonic to D2 event, generating a pervasive tectonic foliation S2, in both the charnockites
and layered tonalitic gneiss. Petrography, field evidence and geochemistry of these foliated
charnockites indicate their igneous nature. The D3 deformation event resulted in plunging
inclined folds on S2 form surface, causing steepening of the foliation. These events were
followed by emplacement of porphyritic hornblende-biotite granite (I-type), chamockitic
veins, sets of veins of pegmatite and fine grained granite.
Introduction
The Orvin-fjella is a roughly N-S oriented, highly rugged mountain range
with very steep faces, situated between mountain ranges of Humboldt on the
east and Muhlig-Hofmann on the west (Fig. 1, inset) in Central Dronning Maud
Land of E.  Antarctica. It  comprises Orvin-I, Orvin-II (Conrad), Orvin-III
(Holtedahl & Drygalski) and Orvin-IV (Filchncr) from east to west. The
geological mapping of Conrad (Orvin II) was taken up as part of ongoing
programme of GSI, during XIV Indian Expedition. The area covered is
bounded by Lat. 71°40'-72°S and Long. 9° 30'- 10°E. The purpose of this
mapping is to : (i) work out the lateral continuity of Humboldt metamorphitcs;
(ii) establish field and structural relationship between mctamorphites and
successive generations of plutonic activity; (iii) petrographic and geochemical
studies to evaluate emplacement history, nature and source of plutonic magma-
tism, and (iv) geochronological studies — for age and regional correlation.
This paper presents the structural relations and petrological studies of rocks
of conrad range.

Geomorphology
Conrad (Orvin-II) is a N-S, 36 km long range, with variable width. It is
characterised by high jagged peaks and steep sides. The highest clevation is
3028 m from M.S.L. The interesting geomorphological feature is that the
western side of the range is flat morainal ground exhibiting instructive morainal
interference pattern (Fig.2), while on the eastern side the polar ice sheet
overrides the range at different levels.
Regional Geological Set-up
As mentioned ear lier the studied area lies between Humboldt and Muhlig-
Hofmann mountain ranges,and the physical continuity is  concealed below the
ice. Further to the west of M uhlig- Hofmann are Gjelsvik fjella and Sverdrup
fjella. All these mountains of Dronning Maud Land are on the eastern side of
Jutulstraumen-Pencksokket Rift zone (J.P.R.Z., Neethling, 1972), which is a 
very significant regiona l structure that separates a Proterozoic platformal
sequence to the west from high grade metamorphic areas to the east. The
geological information from adjoining Gjelsvik fjella, western Muhlig-Hof-
mannfjella and Humboldt mountains are available in details ( cf. Ravich and
Soloviev, 1969; Ravich and Kamenev, 1975; Ohta  et al,  1990 and  references
therein, Ravindra,  et al.,  1994; D'Souza et al„  1995). There is hardly any
geological information available from Orvin f jella. Tingey (1991) while com-
piling the geological map of the Antarctica has shown the Orvin fjella moun-
tains occupied by tw o groups of rocks, namely metamorphites and magmatic
granitoids.
Geology of the Area
The distribution of rock types are presented in Fig.1. The stratigraphic
sequence es tablished on the basis of structures and field relations is as follows:
Pegmatite/Basic dykes (not mappable)
Fine grained granite (as m- scale vein sets)
Coarse grained hbl-b t porphyritic granite (undeformed stock)
Charnockitic veins
Foliated charnockite
Migmatitic hbl-bt gneiss (tonalitic)
Migmatitic hornblende-biotite gneiss:  It is exposed in the southern part of
the area (Fig. 1). The rock is fine to medium grained, grey coloured with strongly
